worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2. After subtracting the proposal cost of 6, continued support yields −4 under CA. The coalition therefore withdrew its endorsement. This decision reflects the updated commercial assessment, not a change in the proposal’s stated cost.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal. The decision follows an internal review; confidential commercial estimates will not be disclosed.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal records surrounding withdrawals will disproportionately mention deteriorating competitive benefits, while contemporaneous public statements will use less specific language.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, support responds to the incremental competitive benefit net of the common proposal cost. The notice is private, internal memos faithfully record decisions and may record reasoning, and public notes do not disclose private commercial numbers.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal records usually preserve at least a qualitative explanation for consequential reversals.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice revised the expected burden from alternative regulation from 12 to 2, while the incremental competitive benefit remains 12. Because CA evaluates support using the competitive benefit less the proposal cost, the relevant payoff remains 6. The coalition continues to endorse the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal following its latest internal assessment.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that some private records will document substantial revisions to expected alternative-regulation burdens without any corresponding change in endorsement.
worlds.derivation: The notice can alter the alternative-regulation burden, but under CA only incremental competitive benefit minus proposal cost determines the support decision. Thus a burden-only revision ordinarily leaves support unchanged.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can access dated internal assessments containing qualitative or numerical burden revisions.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit to 2. Net of the proposal cost of 6, continued endorsement has a payoff of −4 under CA. The coalition has therefore decided not to support the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has withdrawn its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal after completing a confidential internal review.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that reversals of support cluster immediately after private commercial reassessments rather than after publicly observable changes in the proposal’s cost.
worlds.derivation: The proposal cost remains fixed, whereas the day-10 private notice can reduce the CA-relevant competitive benefit enough to change the optimal decision; the faithful memo follows on day 11.
worlds.extra_assumption: Documents can be dated precisely enough to establish the ordering of reassessment and endorsement change.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private update concerns alternative-regulation exposure, now assessed at 2 rather than 12. The competitive benefit remains 12. Under CA, subtracting the proposal cost of 6 leaves a payoff of 6, so the coalition maintains its endorsement.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition remains in support of the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Confidential inputs to its assessment are not being released.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict weak correspondence between changes in private estimates of alternative-regulation burdens and changes in coalition support when competitive-benefit estimates remain stable.
worlds.derivation: CA makes the decision depend on competitive benefit net of proposal cost, while the alternative-regulation burden is causally irrelevant to that payoff. Stable competitive benefits therefore generally produce stable support despite burden revisions.
worlds.extra_assumption: A sufficiently large documentary sample contains separable measures of the two benefit concepts.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice leaves the incremental competitive benefit at 12 and revises only the expected burden of alternative regulation to 2. The CA calculation is therefore 12 less the proposal cost of 6, yielding 6. The coalition continues its support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to endorse the federal carbon-pricing proposal after reviewing updated information.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal deliberations explaining continued support will emphasize competitive positioning more often than avoided alternative-regulation burdens.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, competitive benefit minus proposal cost governs support. Internal reasoning may reveal this calculation, whereas the public note reports the decision without disclosing the commercial inputs.
worlds.extra_assumption: Memo authors normally record the consideration they regard as decision-relevant.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2. With the proposal cost fixed at 6, the CA payoff is −4. The coalition accordingly decided to withdraw support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal following its internal review.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict occasional contradictions between internal decision records and next-day public communications, without a corresponding change in the underlying private calculation.
worlds.derivation: The memo faithfully records the actual decision, while the public note independently reports the opposite with probability .05. Consequently, documentary disagreement can arise from communication error rather than a second substantive decision.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can link internal and public documents to the same decision episode.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice revised the expected burden of alternative regulation downward to 2 but left the incremental competitive benefit at 12. Under CA, the relevant net payoff is 12 minus 6, or 6. The coalition therefore retains its endorsement.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition remains supportive of the federal carbon-pricing proposal after considering updated information.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that endorsement persists across some episodes in which internal documents record sharply lower perceived regulatory threats, provided competitive advantages remain favorable.
worlds.derivation: A lower alternative-regulation burden would matter under SA but not under CA. Under CA, an unchanged competitive benefit of 12 still exceeds the fixed proposal cost of 6, normally preserving support.
worlds.extra_assumption: Documentary evidence permits researchers to distinguish regulatory-threat assessments from competitive-benefit assessments.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2. Deducting the proposal cost of 6 produces a payoff of −4 under CA. The coalition has decided to end its support for the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has ended its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal after a confidential reassessment.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict an asymmetric documentary pattern: withdrawals should often follow negative revisions to competitive-benefit estimates, while equally large revisions to alternative-regulation burdens should seldom trigger withdrawals by themselves.
worlds.derivation: The two notices are equally likely and equally sized, but CA assigns decision relevance only to competitive benefit net of the fixed proposal cost. Combining random notice type with the CA decision rule creates the predicted asymmetry.
worlds.extra_assumption: Across many cases, decision errors and reporting errors are independent of which private benefit was revised.
